NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, heavily dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory — both of which are critical bottlenecks with limited substitutes. On the demand side, NVIDIA derives the vast majority of its Data Center revenue from a concentrated set of hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who are aggressively scaling AI infrastructure investment, creating both enormous revenue opportunity and meaningful customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a world-class product designer and brand owner that outsources manufacturing to a network of specialized Asian suppliers and contract manufacturers while distributing primarily through carriers, retailers, and its own direct channels. Its upstream is dominated by critical semiconductor and display dependencies—particularly TSMC for cutting-edge chips—while its downstream revenue is increasingly diversified between hardware sales through carrier and retail partners and a fast-growing, high-margin Services business tied to platform relationships with companies like Google and Meta.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain, acting as the world's dominant pure-play foundry that manufactures chips designed by fabless companies on equipment sourced from a concentrated set of Western and Japanese toolmakers. Its position is uniquely strategic — almost every leading-edge chip in AI, mobile, and high-performance computing runs through TSMC's fabs — making it both highly dependent on specialized equipment suppliers like ASML and an existential dependency for dozens of the world's largest technology companies.

On the demand side, Micron is increasingly exposed to hyperscalers and AI accelerator vendors—particularly through HBM for NVIDIA's GPU platforms—while maintaining broad diversification across mobile, automotive, and client PC markets.

IREN.supply_chain_summary: IREN Limited sits at the intersection of energy-intensive Bitcoin mining and high-performance AI data center infrastructure, making it critically dependent on upstream GPU suppliers (primarily NVIDIA) and low-cost reliable power sources to maintain competitive hash rates and computing capacity. On the downstream side, IREN's Bitcoin mining revenue is entirely subject to crypto market dynamics and exchange liquidity via platforms like Coinbase, while its emerging AI cloud business targets hyperscaler and enterprise customers seeking GPU compute capacity.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at an early-stage, pre-revenue position in the nuclear power value chain, dependent on a highly specialized upstream ecosystem of uranium enrichers, fuel fabricators, and nuclear-grade component manufacturers to develop and deploy its Aurora microreactor. Downstream, its primary commercial opportunity lies in long-term power purchase agreements with hyperscale data center operators and industrial customers seeking reliable, carbon-free baseload electricity, though all customer relationships remain largely prospective as of 2024.
